module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_regs
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Synchronous MMIO register bank with explicit configuration outputs and readback of counters/status through a compact 64-bit register window.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Decode 16-bit addresses into direct register writes and reads, ignore writes while reset is asserted, and apply write-one-to-clear semantics only to sticky fault/status fields as described by the spec.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Hold configuration fields in flip-flops; sample telemetry inputs synchronously; preserve only explicitly sticky fault state across normal operation until cleared by register action; return to safe defaults on reset.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive all semantic configuration ports directly from registered state, produce deterministic reg_rdata/reg_rvalid on reads, and expose telemetry counters and fault summary for the top-level control path.
ownership_notes: Owns reg_rdata, reg_rvalid, cfg_enable, cfg_mode, cfg_seq_seed, cfg_timeout_thresh, cfg_freshness_thresh, cfg_actuator_min, cfg_actuator_max, cfg_fallback_cmd, cfg_safe_cmd, cfg_velocity_ref, cfg_geometry_id, cfg_queue_enable, cfg_status_clear, and sticky_fault_w1c.
Consumes telemetry and fault-summary inputs without driving them.
Serves as the sole configuration source for request and response control.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_request_fsm
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Compact request formatter and one-outstanding-request controller implemented with synchronous flip-flops and simple bounded control metadata tracking.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: On start_request, capture the current sequence and request descriptors, form a 64-bit request word, assert model_req_valid until accepted, and reject launches while busy unless queueing is enabled.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain a sequence counter, one outstanding descriptor set, launch-cycle metadata, and optional small bounded queue occupancy as control-only state; increment the sequence only on accepted issuance.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive request valid/data toward the external transport, export request_sequence, request_launch_cycle, request_outstanding, request_queue_occupancy, request_accepted_pulse, seq_counter, and busy_reject for downstream validation and telemetry.
ownership_notes: Owns model_req_valid, model_req_data, request_sequence, request_launch_cycle, request_outstanding, request_queue_occupancy, request_accepted_pulse, seq_counter, and busy_reject.
Consumes model_req_ready from the external transport path in the mandatory request direction contract.
Does not implement surrogate computation or any bulk payload storage.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_response_guard
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Response validator and actuator-policy block with timeout watchdog, stale-response filtering, clamping, and deterministic safe fallback selection.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Accept responses only when valid/ready handshake conditions are met, an outstanding request exists, sequence and age checks pass, and encoded policy limits are satisfied; otherwise reject and force fallback when required by policy.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Track current outstanding request metadata, elapsed cycle count relative to launch, last response metadata, sticky fault bits, and the current fallback/safe-mode condition using synchronous control flops only.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive model_rsp_ready back to the external transport, and generate actuator_cmd, actuator_cmd_valid, and safe_mode with safe fallback dominance and min/max clamping applied before output.
ownership_notes: Owns model_rsp_ready, resp_accept_pulse, resp_reject_pulse, resp_stale_pulse, timeout_fault, protocol_fault, sticky_fault_bits, actuator_cmd, actuator_cmd_valid, safe_mode, fallback_active, clamp_event, last_rsp_sequence, last_rsp_age, and last_error_code.
Consumes model_rsp_valid/model_rsp_data from the external transport and request metadata from the request FSM.
Provides the sole described driver for the actuator output path.

fsm_intent.description: A simple issuance controller is implied: idle/busy tracking around one outstanding request, with optional bounded queueing when enabled. The intent is not a complex multi-stage FSM, but a minimal handshake and resource-availability controller.
A simple response-accept/validate/reject control flow is implied, along with a timeout/fallback path. The intent is a compact watchdog-and-validator sequence rather than a deep FSM.

internal_storage: Configuration flops for enable/mode/seed/timeouts/freshness/limits/fallback/safe/reference velocity/geometry ID/queue policy.
Readback decode state and sticky fault control state.
No payload memories, geometry arrays, or surrogate tensors.
output_mapping: Direct registered outputs for configuration fanout.
Address-decoded reg_rdata with reg_rvalid on reads.
Write-one-to-clear control for sticky faults and status clear.

internal_storage: Outstanding-request metadata: sequence and launch cycle.
Busy/queue control metadata implemented with flip-flops only.
Cycle/age tracking relative to request launch.
Last accepted or last observed response metadata.
output_mapping: actuator_cmd and actuator_cmd_valid as the bounded actuator interface.
safe_mode, fault pulses, and error metadata for telemetry and control.

sequencing_notes: The top module remains the single synthesizable integration point and must not be replaced by a register-only or leaf block.
Register writes are ignored while reset is asserted.
Request launches occur only when enabled and resources are available; the sequence counter increments only after accepted request issuance.
At most one request is outstanding unless queueing is explicitly enabled, and any queueing remains bounded and control-only.
Responses are accepted only when valid, current, sequence-matching, and policy-compliant.
Timeout, stale, invalid, mismatched, or protocol-violating responses force fallback behavior when policy requires it.
safe_mode dominates non-safe outputs whenever fallback is active, the controller is disabled, or reset recovery is in effect.
timing_notes: All described logic is synchronous to clk with active-low reset_n.
Handshake decisions are intended to be resolved in a single clock domain with valid/ready semantics.
Timeout and freshness checks are cycle-based and use launch metadata captured at request issuance.
Output commands are clamped before being driven and are only marked valid when an accepted response or safe fallback update is produced.
The architecture avoids multi-cycle hidden dependencies and does not introduce bulk external memories into RTL.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
